The evidence shows that mid-market and enterprise segments outperform SMB/startup segments on retention, satisfaction, expansion, and unit economics:

- **Monthly logo churn** is substantially lower for larger segments: SMB 4.8%, Mid-market 2.1%, Enterprise 1.3% [NL-012#NL-012-S03][NL-015#NL-015-S03][NL-001#NL-001-S04]. The Q2 data explicitly states that "customer satisfaction (NPS) and monthly logo churn metrics improve dramatically in the larger segments" [NL-012#NL-012-S03].
- **NPS** is higher in mid-market (47) and enterprise (52) versus SMB (31) [NL-012#NL-012-S03][NL-015#NL-015-S03][NL-001#NL-001-S04].
- **Expansion revenue** in Q2: SMB $18,000, Mid-market $64,000, Enterprise $91,000, with Enterprise representing 52.6% of all expansion revenue [NL-012#NL-012-S03][NL-012#NL-012-S05][NL-015#NL-015-S03].
- **Revenue concentration**: Mid-market and enterprise accounts combined generate 83.8% of recurring revenue [NL-016#NL-016-S03].
- **Unit economics**: Enterprise LTV:CAC ratio is 16.0x (LTV exceeding $350k) versus SMB's 8.3x (LTV capped at $25k) [NL-016#NL-016-S03].
- **Account value and stability**: Enterprise contracts average $112,000 ACV and are the most valuable segment, with the highest NPS (52) once onboarded [NL-011#NL-011-S08].
- **Official summary**: "The quantitative evidence shows that mid-market and enterprise organizations are our most successful customers" [NL-016#NL-016-S03].
